steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Questionnaires: written questions (closed or open). Strengths: large samples, cheap, anonymous, replicable. Limitations: low response rate, social desirability bias, inflexible.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Interviews: structured, semi-structured, unstructured. Strengths: depth, follow-up, rapport. Limitations: interviewer bias, time-consuming, small samples.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Observations: participant vs non-participant, covert vs overt. Strengths: natural behaviour, ecological validity. Limitations: observer bias, ethical issues, time-consuming. Example: Patrick's Glasgow gang study.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Experiments: lab (rare in sociology), field experiments (e.g. Wood's CV study). Strengths: cause and effect, controlled. Limitations: artificial, ethical issues (deception).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Compare questionnaires and interviews, evaluating strengths and limitations of each. | Explain why a sociologist might choose participant observation, and evaluate its ethical implications. | A researcher wants to study whether employers discriminate against ethnic minority applicants. Which method is most appropriate?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Questionnaires: large samples, cheap, anonymous (strengths); low response, social desirability, inflexible (limitations). Interviews: depth, follow-ups (strengths); interviewer bias, small samples (li | Participant observation: useful for deviant/closed groups. Ethical issues: covert = deception (violates consent) but may be only way to access some groups; overt = honest but Hawthorne effect. | A field experiment (CV study like Wood's): send identical CVs varying only ethnic name. Tests actual behaviour, high ecological validity, can establish causation. Ethical issue: deception of employers

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Questionnaires = BROAD + SHALLOW. Interviews = NARROW + DEEP. Participant observation: best for CLOSED GROUPS. Covert = deception but access. Overt = honest but reactivity. Field experiment (CV study): best for testing DISCRIMINATION.
